verses.zh: 我又看见一个新天新地；因为先前的天地已经过去了，海也不再有了。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and earth had ceased to exist,[NOTE:2] and the sea existed no more.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
For the translation of ἀπέρχομαι (aperchomai; here ἀπῆλθαν [apēlthan]) L&N 13.93 has “to go out of existence—‘to cease to exist, to pass away, to cease.’”

verses.zh: 我又看见圣城新耶路撒冷由　神那里从天而降，预备好了，就如新妇妆饰整齐，等候丈夫。
verses.en: And I saw the holy city—the new Jerusalem—descending out of heaven from God, made ready like a bride adorned for her husband.

verses.zh: 我听见有大声音从宝座出来说：「看哪，　神的帐幕在人间。他要与人同住，他们要作他的子民。　神要亲自与他们同在，作他们的　神。
verses.en: And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying: “Look! The residence[NOTE:1] of God is among human beings.[NOTE:2] He[NOTE:3] will live among them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “dwelling place”; traditionally, “tabernacle”; literally “tent.”

Or “people”; Grk “men” (ἀνθρώπων, anthrōpōn), a generic use of the term. In the translation “human beings” was used here because “people” occurs later in the verse and translates a different Greek word (λαοί, laoi).
Grk “men, and he.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.

‡ Most mss (א MK) do not add the words “[as] their God” (αὐτῶν θεός, autōn theos) after “he will be with them.” The mss with these words include A 2030 2050 2329 al. The Andreas group (MA) also has the words, but in a different arrangement with the preceding (ἔσται μετ᾿ αὐτῶν θεὸς αὐτῶν, estai met’ autōn theos autōn). Not only do the words float, but scribes may have been motivated to make a connection here more directly with Isa 7:14; 8:8; Jer 24:7; 31:33; Zech 8:8. In light of sufficient external evidence as well as the possibility that the longer reading is theologically motivated, the shorter reading is preferred. NA28 places the words in brackets, indicating doubts as to their authenticity.

verses.zh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛，因为以前的事都过去了。」
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death will not exist any more—or mourning, or crying, or pain, for the former things have ceased to exist.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “God, and he.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation. Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
For the translation of ἀπέρχομαι (aperchomai; here ἀπῆλθαν [apēlthan]) L&N 13.93 has “to go out of existence—‘to cease to exist, to pass away, to cease.’”

verses.zh: 坐宝座的说：「看哪，我将一切都更新了！」又说：「你要写上；因这些话是可信的，是真实的。」
verses.en: And the one seated on the throne said: “Look! I am making all things new!” Then[NOTE:1] he said to me, “Write it down,[NOTE:2] because these words are reliable[NOTE:3] and true.”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.
The words “it down” are not in the Greek text, but are implied. Direct objects were frequently omitted in Greek when clear from the context.
Grk “faithful.”

verses.zh: 他又对我说：「都成了！我是阿拉法，我是俄梅戛；我是初，我是终。我要将生命泉的水白白赐给那口渴的人喝。
verses.en: He also said to me, “It is done![NOTE:1] I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. To the one who is thirsty I will give water[NOTE:2] free of charge[NOTE:3] from the spring of the water of life.
notes: Or “It has happened.”
The word “water” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. Direct objects were frequently omitted in Greek when clear from the context.
Or “as a free gift” (see L&N 57.85).

verses.zh: 得胜的，必承受这些为业：我要作他的　神，他要作我的儿子。
verses.en: The one who conquers[NOTE:1] will inherit these things, and I will be his God and he will be my son.
notes: Or “who is victorious”; traditionally, “who overcomes.”

verses.zh: 惟有胆怯的、不信的、可憎的、杀人的、淫乱的、行邪术的、拜偶像的，和一切说谎话的，他们的分就在烧着硫磺的火湖里；这是第二次的死。」
verses.en: But as for the cowards, unbelievers, detestable persons, murderers, the sexually immoral, and those who practice magic spells,[NOTE:1] idol worshipers,[NOTE:2] and all those who lie, their place[NOTE:3] will be in the lake that burns with fire and sulfur.[NOTE:4] That[NOTE:5] is the second death.”
notes: On the term φαρμακεία (pharmakeia, “magic spells”) see L&N 53.100: “the use of magic, often involving drugs and the casting of spells upon people—‘to practice magic, to cast spells upon, to engage in sorcery, magic, sorcery.’ φαρμακεία: ἐν τῇ φαρμακείᾳ σου ἐπλανήθησαν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ‘with your magic spells you deceived all the peoples (of the world)’ Re 18:23.”
Grk “idolaters.”
Grk “their share.”
Traditionally, “brimstone.”

Grk “sulfur, which is.” The relative pronoun has been translated as “that” to indicate its connection to the previous clause. The nearest logical antecedent is “the lake [that burns with fire and sulfur],” although “lake” (λίμνη, limnē) is feminine gender, while the pronoun “which” (ὅ, ho) is neuter gender. This means that (1) the proper antecedent could be “their place” (Grk “their share,”) agreeing with the relative pronoun in number and gender, or (2) the neuter pronoun still has as its antecedent the feminine noun “lake,” since agreement in gender between pronoun and antecedent was not always maintained, with an explanatory phrase occurring with a neuter pronoun regardless of the case of the antecedent. In favor of the latter explanation is Rev 20:14, where the phrase “the lake of fire” is in apposition to the phrase “the second death.”

verses.zh: 拿着七个金碗、盛满末后七灾的七位天使中，有一位来对我说：「你到这里来，我要将新妇，就是羔羊的妻，指给你看。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the seven final plagues came and spoke to me,[NOTE:2] saying, “Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb!”
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.

Grk “with me.” The translation “with me” implies that John was engaged in a dialogue with the one speaking to him (e.g., Jesus or an angel) when in reality it was a one-sided conversation, with John doing all the listening. For this reason, μετ᾿ ἐμοῦ (met’ emou, “with me”) was translated as “to me.” See also v. 15.

verses.zh: 我被圣灵感动，天使就带我到一座高大的山，将那由　神那里、从天而降的圣城耶路撒冷指示我。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] he took me away in the Spirit[NOTE:2] to a huge, majestic mountain[NOTE:3] and showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the angel’s invitation.

Or “in the spirit.” “Spirit” could refer either to the Holy Spirit or the human spirit, but in either case John was in “a state of spiritual exaltation best described as a trance” (R. H. Mounce, Revelation [NICNT], 75).
Grk “to a mountain great and high.”

verses.zh: 城中有　神的荣耀；城的光辉如同极贵的宝石，好像碧玉，明如水晶。
verses.en: The city possesses[NOTE:1] the glory of God; its brilliance is like a precious jewel, like a stone of crystal-clear jasper.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “from God, having the glory of God.” Here a new sentence was started in the translation by supplying the words “the city” to refer back to the previous clause and translating the participle (“having”) as a finite verb.

On the term ἰάσπιδι (iaspidi) BDAG 465 s.v. ἴασπις states, “jasper, a precious stone found in various colors, mostly reddish, somet. green…brown, blue, yellow, and white. In antiquity the name was not limited to the variety of quartz now called jasper, but could designate any opaque precious stone. Rv 21:18f. W. λίθος 4:3 (TestSol C 11:8). λίθος ἴασπις κρυσταλλίζων a stone of crystal-clear jasper 21:11 (cp. Is 54:12); perh. the opal is meant here; acc. to some, the diamond.”

verses.zh: 有高大的墙，有十二个门，门上有十二位天使，门上又写着以色列十二个支派的名字。
verses.en: It has[NOTE:1] a massive, high wall[NOTE:2] with twelve gates,[NOTE:3] with twelve angels at the gates, and the names of the twelve tribes of the nation of Israel[NOTE:4] are written on the gates.[NOTE:5]
notes: Grk “jasper, having.” Here a new sentence was started in the translation.
Grk “a (city) wall great and high.”

On this term BDAG 897 s.v. πυλών 1 states, “gate, esp. of the large, impressive gateways at the entrance of temples and palaces…of the entrances of the heavenly Jerusalem…οἱ πυλῶνες αὐτῆς οὐ μὴ κλεισθῶσιν its entrances shall never be shut Rv 21:25; cp. vss. 12ab, 13abcd, 15, 21ab; 22:14.”
Grk “of the sons of Israel.” The translation “nation of Israel” is given in L&N 11.58.
Grk “on them”; the referent (the gates) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 东边有三门，北边有三门，南边有三门，西边有三门。
verses.en: There are[NOTE:1] three gates on the east side, three gates on the north side, three gates on the south side, and three gates on the west side.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “There are” have been supplied to make a complete English sentence. This is a continuation of the previous sentence, a lengthy and complicated one in Greek.
The word “side” has been supplied four times in this verse for clarity.

verses.zh: 城墙有十二根基，根基上有羔羊十二使徒的名字。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] wall of the city has twelve foundations, and on them are the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

verses.zh: 对我说话的，拿着金苇子当尺，要量那城和城门城墙。
verses.en: The angel[NOTE:1] who spoke to me had a golden measuring rod with which to measure the city and its foundation stones and wall.
notes: Grk “the one”; the referent (the angel of v. 9) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 城是四方的，长宽一样。天使用苇子量那城，共有四千里，长、宽、高都是一样；
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] the city is laid out as a square,[NOTE:2] its length and width the same. He[NOTE:3] measured the city with the measuring rod[NOTE:4] at 1,400 miles[NOTE:5] (its length and width and height are equal).
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the somewhat parenthetical nature of the description of the city.
Or “the city lies square.” On κεῖμαι (keimai) in this context, BDAG 537 s.v. 2 states, “lie, of things…ἡ πόλις τετράγωνος κεῖται is laid out as a square Rv 21:16.”
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Grk “with the rod”; the word “measuring” is supplied from the description in v. 15.
Or “2,200 kilometers,” Grk “12,000 stades.” A stade was a measure of length about 607 ft (185 m).

verses.zh: 又量了城墙，按着人的尺寸，就是天使的尺寸，共有一百四十四肘。
verses.en: He also measured its wall, 144 cubits[NOTE:1] according to human measurement, which is also the angel’s.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here the measurement was kept in cubits in the translation because of the possible symbolic significance of the number 144 (12 times 12). This is about 216 ft (65 m).

Here L&N 81.1 translate the phrase μέτρον ἀνθρώπου, ὅ ἐστιν ἀγγέλου (metron anthrōpou, ho estin angelou) “‘the unit of measurement used by a person, that is, by an angel’ Re 21:17.” It is more likely that μέτρον is an accusative of respect or reference.

verses.zh: 墙是碧玉造的；城是精金的，如同明净的玻璃。
verses.en: The city’s[NOTE:1] wall is made[NOTE:2] of jasper and the city is pure gold, like transparent glass.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “and its wall”; the referent of the pronoun (the city) has been specified in the translation for clarity. Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

The phrase ἡ ἐνδώμησις τοῦ τείχους (hē endōmēsis tou teichous) is difficult to translate precisely. BDAG 334 s.v. ἐνδώμησις states, “primary mng. ‘interior structure’; in our lit. prob.=construction, hence material τοῦ τείχους Rv 21:18.” The phrase could then be translated, “the foundation of the city wall was jasper” or “the material used for the wall of the city was jasper.” The latter alternative has been used in the translation because the text goes on to discuss the foundation in 21:19 (using the term θεμέλιος [themelios]), which is somewhat redundant if the foundation is mentioned here.

Or “transparent crystal.” See L&N 6.222, which notes the emphasis is on transparency here. The same Greek word, καθαρός (katharos), means both “pure” (referring to the gold) and “transparent” (referring to the glass).

verses.zh: 城墙的根基是用各样宝石修饰的：第一根基是碧玉；第二是蓝宝石；第三是绿玛瑙；第四是绿宝石；
verses.en: The foundations of the city’s wall are decorated[NOTE:1] with every kind of precious stone. The first foundation is jasper, the second sapphire, the third agate,[NOTE:2] the fourth emerald,
notes: The perfect participle here has been translated as an intensive (resultative) perfect.
Agate (also called chalcedony) is a semiprecious stone usually milky or gray in color (L&N 2.32).

verses.zh: 第五是红玛瑙；第六是红宝石；第七是黄璧玺；第八是水苍玉；第九是红璧玺；第十是翡翠；第十一是紫玛瑙；第十二是紫晶。
verses.en: the fifth onyx,[NOTE:1] the sixth carnelian,[NOTE:2] the seventh chrysolite,[NOTE:3] the eighth beryl,[NOTE:4] the ninth topaz, the tenth chrysoprase,[NOTE:5] the eleventh jacinth,[NOTE:6] and the twelfth amethyst.
notes: Onyx (also called sardonyx) is a semiprecious stone that comes in various colors (L&N 2.35).
Carnelian is a semiprecious gemstone, usually red in color (L&N 2.36).
Chrysolite refers to either quartz or topaz, golden yellow in color (L&N 2.37).
Beryl is a semiprecious stone, usually blue-green or green in color (L&N 2.38).
Chrysoprase is a greenish type of quartz (L&N 2.40).
Jacinth is a semiprecious stone, probably blue in color (also called “hyacinth,” but that translation is not used here because of possible confusion with the flower of the same name). See L&N 2.41.

verses.zh: 十二个门是十二颗珍珠，每门是一颗珍珠。城内的街道是精金，好像明透的玻璃。
verses.en: And the twelve gates are twelve pearls—each one of the gates is made from just one pearl! The[NOTE:1] main street[NOTE:2] of the city is pure gold, like transparent glass.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
The Greek word πλατεῖα (plateia) refers to a major (broad) street (L&N 1.103).

verses.zh: 我未见城内有殿，因主　神―全能者和羔羊为城的殿。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] I saw no temple in the city, because the Lord God—the All-Powerful[NOTE:2]—and the Lamb are its temple.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic. Every verse from here to the end of this chapter begins with καί in Greek, but due to differences between Greek and contemporary English style, these have not been translated.
On this word BDAG 755 s.v. παντοκράτωρ states, “the Almighty, All-Powerful, Omnipotent (One) only of God…(ὁ) κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ π.…Rv 1:8; 4:8; 11:17; 15:3; 16:7; 21:22.”

verses.zh: 那城内又不用日月光照；因有　神的荣耀光照，又有羔羊为城的灯。
verses.en: The city does not need the sun or the moon to shine on it, because the glory of God lights it up, and its lamp is the Lamb.

verses.zh: 列国要在城的光里行走；地上的君王必将自己的荣耀归与那城。
verses.en: The nations[NOTE:1] will walk by its light, and the kings of the earth will bring their grandeur[NOTE:2] into it.
notes: Or “the Gentiles” (the same Greek word may be translated “Gentiles” or “nations”).
Or “splendor”; Grk “glory.”

verses.zh: 城门白昼总不关闭，在那里原没有黑夜。
verses.en: Its gates will never be closed during the day[NOTE:1] (and[NOTE:2] there will be no night there).[NOTE:3]
notes: On the translation “during the day” see BDAG 436 s.v. ἡμέρα 1.a, “But also, as in Thu. et al., of time within which someth. occurs, ἡμέρας during the day Rv 21:25.”

The Greek connective γάρ (gar) most often expresses some sort of causal connection. However, in this context there is no causal force to the second phrase; γάρ simply expresses continuation or connection. Because of this it has been translated as “and.” See BDAG 189-90 s.v. 2.
The clause has virtually the force of a parenthetical comment.

verses.zh: 人必将列国的荣耀、尊贵归与那城。
verses.en: They will bring the grandeur and the wealth[NOTE:1] of the nations[NOTE:2] into it,
notes: Grk “honor,” but BDAG 1005 s.v. τιμή 2.b states, “An outstanding feature of the use of τ., as already shown in several passages, is its combination w. δόξα…of earthly possessions τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν Rv 21:26 (τιμή concr.=an object of value: Ezk 22:25).”
Or “the Gentiles” (the same Greek word may be translated “Gentiles” or “nations”).

verses.zh: 凡不洁净的，并那行可憎与虚谎之事的，总不得进那城；只有名字写在羔羊生命册上的才得进去。
verses.en: but[NOTE:1] nothing ritually unclean[NOTE:2] will ever enter into it, nor anyone who does what is detestable[NOTE:3] or practices falsehood,[NOTE:4] but only those whose names[NOTE:5] are written in the Lamb’s book of life.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.
Here BDAG 552 s.v. κοινός 2 states, “pert. to being of little value because of being common, common, ordinary, profane…b. specifically, of that which is ceremonially impure: Rv 21:27.”
Or “what is abhorrent”; Grk “who practices abominations.”

Grk “practicing abomination or falsehood.” Because of the way βδέλυγμα (bdelugma) has been translated (“does what is detestable”) it was necessary to repeat the idea from the participle ποιῶν (poiōn, “practices”) before the term “falsehood.” On this term, BDAG 1097 s.v. ψεῦδος states, “ποιεῖν ψεῦδος practice (the things that go with) falsehood Rv 21:27; 22:15.” Cf. Rev 3:9.
Grk “those who are written”; the word “names” is implied.
